doc.title: Mr. and Mrs. A.C. Synigal Interview, 1962-05-24

title: Moving to New Orleans, sewing with her mother, marriage and children
summary: After her father's death at 14 the family moved to New Orleans and she sewed costumes with her mother; she talks of her marriage and four children.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: And things were going on just as nice and nobody. My mother came in here and we lived on Priya. Priya, the Wogan's. You know where the Wogan's live? On Priya and Espinade? Those are very old, rich people. On Espinade and Priya. And my mother came here and I don't know how it came with the neighbors and all. They told the Wogan's that my mother was a modi. So, she starts running right away. Being a neighbor, she went to see. Then they sent it to different ones and all. Then I was 14 when my father died. We moved here and I began sewing with her. And I sewed with her practically until she died. I'm making all those beautiful queen maid's costumes and made good money. See, she came right in here. Of course, good money in those days. But my, I, as we went on, and then for years and years I sewed with my mother until I married my first husband. He was Victor Serena. And, well, I didn't sew while I was mad. I just did a little to help her because I began having children. I had four children for him. And so, of course, I had to keep house and take care of him. But I would help her when she'd get too much work. You know, I'd go around and help her. So, but my husband had a terrible accident. His death, he was drowned. He was drowned and, and, of course, that's what's so sad. Just broke up my home life. I went to live with my mother. And then I began sewing. Really had to sew then to help my children and my mother. She was a widow. My mother was a widow, so we were together. And I stayed eight years a widow when he came along. When he came along. That was the end of eight years. That was the end of eight years. And he was a widow three years, huh? Your wife was dead three years. And we brought the family together. He had three or four children. I had three. Three children.

And I had four. And you can buy them. And they'd sell them. And, oh, everybody was talking. I said, how are you all going to do that? Big family, get it together. And he was an insurance man then, making good money. And I was making good money. So, when only, we made it. I said, like a lady, a friend of mine, she's married a second time. And her husband has one little girl, 14 years old. So, she came here crying on my shoulder. Oh, I made a terrible mistake. I said, what do you mean? What do you mean? She says, oh, I don't know. I made a terrible mistake. That little girl is about to send me crazy. 14 years old. She's about to send me crazy. I said, what? Send me crazy? Well, suppose you had seven, huh? Four and three. Seven like I did. I said, suppose you'd have seven like I did. And then had to work too. I said, of course you had to. She's an Avon. She's an Avon specialist. She's the head of all Avons in New Orleans. And a wonderful job like you have. And worried about one little girl. She said, but that little girl is not anybody crazy. I said, she wouldn't send me crazy. Because I let her know who is boss. So, she said, I tried to do that. But he just spoiled me. You know, that's his only child. He just spoiled her. I said, well, spoil him and spoil her too. But let them know when it's time, you know, to be. So, finally, she went home and she said, I did what you said, Ms. Sengal. I said, well, what happened? Everything is okidokid. I let them know I was boss. I said, well, that's what you had to do. So, everything is going on nicely. So, um.
